note: The reported symptom is 'crashes DXC without providing an error message', and the issue is labelled crash. Per SKILL.md, anything crash-shaped uses internal_failure, which is judged on exit STATUS first and text markers only as a backstop. That matters here in both directions. (a) The same defect wears different clothes across builds: the Debug ground truth exits 0xE0000001 with 'Internal compiler error: LLVM Assert' (the C++-exception assert form, not the 0x80000003 trap form), while the shipping Release binaries have asserts compiled out and fail some other way or not at all -- a predicate keyed to 'LLVM Assert' would score every release clean and manufacture a false 'fixed'. (b) The shader in this issue is INVALID, so the correct behaviour is a diagnostic, and dxc returns E_FAIL (0x80004005) for ordinary diagnosed errors. A 'nonzero_exit' predicate would therefore score a correctly-diagnosing compiler as reproducing the crash -- inventing the bug rather than missing it. internal_failure explicitly excludes E_FAIL unless a text marker fires. Control: control-valid.hlsl is the same shader with the three invalid resource constructs removed (blur returns float4, no local RWTexture2D, no assignment to the global); it compiles clean and the predicate must not fire on it -- captured as variant-control-valid-main-debug.txt with --expect no-match.
